<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `680045a767cc7b38ea41869469270f4b7639d495` — the merge of head `67101a94735ab425a1fd82d8c4428389f6e00444` into base `bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 680045a767cc7b38ea41869469270f4b7639d495 && git checkout 680045a767cc7b38ea41869469270f4b7639d495
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 67101a94735ab425a1fd82d8c4428389f6e00444 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 && git merge --no-ff 67101a94735ab425a1fd82d8c4428389f6e00444

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**ACCEPT** · PR #32917 · head `67101a94735ab425a1fd82d8c4428389f6e00444` · 2026-11-13T00:05Z · `Fixes #32732`

## 席位核对

1. **Shape:** draft PR to `main`, `Fixes #32732` alone. Path surface (read from the file list): `packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts`, its test file, one changeset (`@objectstack/objectql`: patch). No governed path, no `packages/spec/src/**`; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no narrowing declaration. No contract-review face is touched: CI plus this seat read. Tier S.
2. **Premise measured:** on `main`, `writeUnlessMovedSince` answered `'moved'` for any other stamp and the caller counted the row under `concurrentRows`, trusting the moving write. The diff keeps the conditional write (same name, so the reader ledger row of `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` holds) and adds `fillRowUnlessMovedSince`: on `moved`, the re-read row is computed by the walk's own `computePage` and judged by `judgeRow` (the walk's per-row predicate lifted out unchanged, read line by line against the removed loop body); owes nothing ⇒ `moved`; owes ⇒ ONE conditional write under the new stamp; blocked or moved again ⇒ `left` → `report.failures`. Counting is bumped after the retry settles, as before; a transient retry re-enters from the first write and re-judges, so it stays idempotent.
3. **Gates:** check-runs on this head: 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending; local whole-package objectql 590/590 files, 66 derived families + `pnpm lint` exit 0, `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED (PR body).
4. **Negative pins ablated:** answering `moved` without the re-judgement turns the four `[#32732]` cases red (quoted in the PR); the CONTROL (#32527 engine-write case, now also asserting the fill wrote nothing over it) stays green.
5. **Prose checked sentence by sentence:** the changeset's first paragraph (moved row read again and judged under the live definition; holds ⇒ `concurrentRows`; owes ⇒ written under its new stamp with the same precondition; moves again or blocked ⇒ `failures`, `stored-expression-fill-incomplete`, exit 1; the same-stamp fallback warns once per object) and second paragraph (`concurrentRows` a required member of both exported report types since the conditional writes of PR #32690; a row deleted mid-walk counted there) agree with the diff. The report shape is unchanged: no exported member added or removed, docblocks only.
6. **Out of scope:** the card's prose nits outside the claimed surface (`protocol-stored-expression-fill.ts` notice wording, `engine-insert.ts` one-time warning, `concurrent-update-error.ts` / `engine-top-level.ts` comments, `cli.mdx` row) stay in Acceptance notes; they change no behaviour. Seat nit, accepted: under `changed: false` a moved row still holding a stale (non-NULL) value is counted under `concurrentRows`, the same scope the walk itself applies to an unmoved row.
- **Landing:** Tier S path, `Clause-②: no`. K = 10 commits behind `main` (< 15), no new language pack: no merge needed. Landed by the seat under the maintainer's standing word (「所有车道座位，应该使用pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地 pr」) and the 18.4.0 amendment (「已经在开发的 p2 可以继续跟进到 合并」).
